title: Ferguson's Dirichlet Process Breakthrough: A Lasting Legacy
summary: Ferguson's 1973 introduction of the Dirichlet process marked a breakthrough in Bayesian nonparametric statistics. For the first time, a prior on the space of probability measures fulfilled two key desiderata: large support and analytical tractability. In this paper, we review three complementary constructions of the Dirichlet process, whose roots can be traced back to Ferguson: through finite-dimensional distributions, via normalization of a gamma process, and through predictive distributions.
